svg.title: H100 memory hardware: register pool, L1 and shared memory, L2, and HBM
svg.desc: Scope diagram for H100 SXM memory hardware. Each SM has 65,536 32-bit registers and 256 KB of combined L1 cache and shared-memory capacity. L1 automatically caches eligible accesses; shared memory is explicitly used cooperative storage, with up to 228 KB per SM carved from the combined capacity. A 50 MB L2 cache is shared across the GPU and connects to 80 GB HBM3. Lines show common data exchange, not a mandatory path through every storage level.

g.text: H100 memory hardware: capacity, scope, and purpose
Reference: full H100 SXM 80 GB. Memory levels have different roles and sharing scopes.
Inside each SM: on-chip working storage
Register pool: 65,536 × 32-bit = 262,144 bytes per SM
Stores live operands, intermediate values, addresses, and accumulators.
Values belong to execution contexts; allocation uses a fixed SM-wide register capacity.
Registers are direct working storage, rather than an automatically managed cache.
Eligible cached
device-data access
Explicit reads
and writes
One combined capacity: 256 KB per SM for L1 cache + shared memory
L1 cache: automatically managed
Caches eligible accesses near the compute units.
Cache policy can allow bypassing L1.
Shared memory: explicit cooperative storage
Up to 228 KB per SM, carved from this capacity.
Allocation changes the capacity left for L1.
Cached device-memory traffic
L2 cache: 50 MB, shared across the full GPU
Automatically caches device-memory traffic from many SMs.
A cache hit can serve data without another access to HBM.
Device-memory traffic
HBM3: 80 GB of high-bandwidth device memory
Large backing storage for data; physically separate from the SMs and on-chip caches.
Rated bandwidth: 3.35 TB/s. Much larger than on-chip storage, with higher access latency.
Read the picture: registers and L1/shared memory belong to each SM; L2 and HBM serve the GPU.
Lines show common data exchange. An access does not have to visit every level shown.
Shared memory is explicitly used storage; it is not another automatic cache between L1 and registers.
